After investigating potential challenges to the initial verdict, I found:

H1 (Restatements/Corrections): NO_RELEVANT_EVIDENCE - The retrieved evidence (E11, E12, E13) shows the same net sales figures ($143,756M for Q1 2026 and $124,300M for Q1 2025) with no mention of any restatements, corrections, or adjustments to these figures.

H2 (One-time items/Accounting changes): NO_RELEVANT_EVIDENCE - Evidence E14 discusses litigation matters unrelated to revenue. E15 and E16 discuss ASU 2025-06, an accounting standard for internal-use software that will be effective in Q1 2029, not Q1 2026. None of these indicate any one-time items or accounting changes that affected the Q1 2026 revenue comparison.

H3 (Different quarter lengths): CHALLENGE_REFUTED - Evidence E17 and E18 explicitly state that "The Company's fiscal years 2025 and 2024 spanned 52 weeks each," confirming that both quarters being compared had the same number of weeks, ensuring comparability.

The evidence review confirms that E1, E3, and E11 all ENTAIL the claim, showing total net sales of $143,756M for Q1 2026 vs $124,300M for Q1 2025, representing a 16% increase, which exceeds the 15% threshold stated in the claim. No contradicting evidence was found. The verdict remains SUPPORTED.
